small_guidance:
- Add larger autotune configs now that BLOCK_M=128,BLOCK_N=128,BLOCK_K=16 is known to compile: try BLOCK_M=128,BLOCK_N=256,BLOCK_K=16 and BLOCK_M=256,BLOCK_N=128,BLOCK_K=16 at num_warps=8, num_stages=2; also add BLOCK_K=32 variants with num_stages=3 for better K-pipeline overlap given the 4× duplicated dot per iteration.
- Swap program-id ordering so pid_sp is the fastest axis (or use a pid-swizzle on (OC tile, sp tile)) to improve L2 reuse of weights across spatial tiles within the same N — currently weights are reloaded per spatial tile with no L2 locality benefit from the launch grid.
- Hoist the weight load out of the K-loop body into a single tl.dot per K-tile and reuse it across the 4 (x00,x01,x10,x11) loads (already done) — additionally precompute `ih_base*IW + iw_base` once and reuse via pointer adds; consider reading weights through `tl.load` with `eviction_policy='evict_last'` and inputs with `evict_first` to keep W resident.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a single fused im2col-GEMM where each program produces a tile of pooled outputs directly: GEMM-M = OC, GEMM-N = pooled spatial tile, and inside each program compute the 2×2 pre-pool conv outputs by issuing 4 dots sharing the same W tile (current design) but switch the K-loop to load W once per K-step and accumulate into a single [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, 4] register block via separate dots — verify the compiler reuses W in registers; if not, manually unroll KH·KW so weights sit in registers across all 4 pool positions.
- Move to NHWC (channels_last) input layout so the K reduction (IC × KH × KW) has IC as the contiguous axis; this turns the x gather into 4 contiguous vector loads of length BLOCK_K per (kh,kw) and removes the strided IH*IW jumps that currently hurt memory throughput.
- Consider a persistent-CTA scheme keyed on (N·OC_tile) with the spatial tile iterated inside the kernel, amortizing weight loads across all spatial tiles for a given (N, OC tile); given OC=128 and small KH·KW=3·3·64=576, the entire weight slab for one OC tile fits easily in SMEM/registers and can be loaded once per program.
